title: Production AI Agent Platform
summary: The major portfolio project. Combine structured outputs, token-aware context management, retrieval, idempotent tool calling, a bounded agent loop, retry/fallback reliability, and evaluation into one system with an architecture diagram, implementation, tests, and README.
requirements: Combine structured-output validation, token-budget-aware context assembly, threshold-gated retrieval, idempotent tool execution, a bounded agent loop, retry-with-fallback reliability, and a labeled eval set into one system.
Provide an architecture diagram or written design doc.
Provide a README explaining design decisions.
Document at least 3 concrete failure scenarios and how the system handles each.
Record an eval baseline and demonstrate a regression check.
start: Pick one coherent scenario, e.g. a documentation support bot or an internal Q&A agent, don't demo each module's concept as an unrelated add-on, they should work together as one system the way they do in Module 8's capstone.
acceptance: Model output going into any downstream logic is repaired and schema-validated first.
Context sent to the model stays within a computed token budget.
Retrieval applies a real relevance threshold, with an honest 'no answer' path when nothing clears it.
At least one tool call is idempotency-key protected.
The agent's control flow (if any) has a hard step limit and stuck-detection.
At least one model call has retry+backoff+fallback.
An eval set with a recorded baseline demonstrates at least one regression catch (a deliberately worse version scoring lower).
tests: End-to-end happy path succeeds and produces a well-formed final answer.
A query with no relevant KB match returns an honest 'no answer' rather than a confident guess.
A duplicate tool call (same call ID) doesn't double-execute its side effect.
An injected model-API failure triggers retry then fallback without crashing the request.
Running the eval suite against a deliberately-regressed version (e.g. no threshold) shows a lower score than the baseline.
mistakes: Building each module's feature as an isolated demo instead of one integrated pipeline.
Skipping tests for the 'boring' parts (schema validation, idempotency) in favor of only testing the interesting failure paths.
An architecture diagram or README that doesn't match what the code actually does.
solution: This is intentionally the least prescriptive project, the previous 7 projects and the Module 8 capstone exercise are your reference implementations for each individual piece, the work here is INTEGRATING them into one coherent, documented system, not inventing new techniques.
